description: The word "utopia" means both a "good place" and "no place." Utopian literature embraces this duality by imagining places better than our own. This seminar will begin with these literary utopias before considering historical attempts to make a "good place" in a real place and time. We'll investigate the common problems that both real and imagined utopias have tried to solve, and well seek to understand the roots of these problems. Writing for the course will emphasize research, analysis, argumentation, and reflection.
